title: The return of the wolf
text: When wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone in 1995, rangers expected fewer elk. They got a different river. The elk, hunted again after seventy safe years, stopped {{1}} the open valleys and moved to higher ground; young willows and aspens, untouched for decades, shot up; songbirds nested in the new growth; beavers, who need willows, returned and built dams, and the dams created ponds that {{2}} frogs, fish and otters. Even the rivers changed: with banks {{3}} by roots, erosion slowed and channels deepened. Ecologists call this a trophic cascade — predators {{4}} behaviour all the way down the food chain — and Yellowstone became its textbook {{5}}. The story comes with scholarly {{6}}: the recovery is real, but not every change has a single cause, and drought played its part alongside the wolves. That {{7}} makes the lesson more useful, not less: ecosystems are woven tight enough that removing one thread can quietly {{8}} the whole cloth. Wolves were never a magic fix; they were the missing piece that let everything already present reconnect.

gaps.explanation: 'stopped grazing the open valleys' — feeding on the vegetation there; gaze takes 'at', grope takes 'for'.
'ponds that harboured frogs, fish and otters' — sheltered them; holler = shout, huddle = crowd together.
'banks anchored by roots' — held firmly in place; angle = tilt, armour = provide a metal shell.
'predators steer behaviour all the way down the chain' — direct it; sneer = mock, shear = cut wool.
'Yellowstone became its textbook case' — the standard example; course, costume and custom do not complete the phrase.
'comes with scholarly caveats' — qualifications to the claim; cravat = a neck scarf, coupon = a voucher.

gaps.hint: the state of not being sure (noun)
gaps.explanation: 'that uncertainty makes the lesson more useful' — the acknowledged doubt teaches humility; urgency = pressing importance.
'removing one thread can quietly unpick the whole cloth' — undo the weaving; uproot = tear a plant from the ground, upholster = cover furniture.
